t.E442.agn: In its 2016 re-evaluation EFSA saw no need to change the existing acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 30 mg/kg body weight and found no safety concern for its use as a food additive.
t.E442.body: It breaks down in digestive fluids, releasing phosphate. In rats about 79% of the labelled substance was excreted in faeces and 4% in urine within 24 hours; the absorbed phosphate was found in bone and muscle as inorganic phosphate.
t.E442.prod: It is produced by modifying a plant raw material through a chemical reaction.
t.E442.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI of 30 mg/kg body weight per day maintained, no safety concern.
t.E442.summary: A synthetic emulsifier produced from fats. It is used in chocolate instead of lecithin to improve flow.
t.E442.what: It is an emulsifier that adjusts the flow (viscosity) of chocolate.
